_status: DRAFT 2026-11-13. NOT registered, NOT collected. See news_drift_v1.DRAFT.json: same rules about editing, same twin relationship.
purpose: Does a large one-day move WITHOUT news and WITHOUT a sector reason partly reverse over 5 days (liquidity-driven moves mean-revert; Chan 2003 covers small caps, the large-cap test is the new part)? Leg 2 of plan B4. Together the two legs replace weekly_reversal_v1.
event_rule: At the close of the signal day: stock return minus SPY at least +5% or at most -5%, AND no company headline in the window of news_drift_v1 (same providers, same text rule), AND the stock's return minus its sector ETF's return has the SAME sign and a size of at least 4%. The sector residual removes sympathy moves (AMD falls because NVDA guided down: no AMD headline, yet fundamental).
signal_rule: Direction opposes the move: a rise gives short (-1), a fall gives long (+1). Same liquidity filter and emission as news_drift_v1.

pass_all_of: mean net excess at 5 days above 0.3% after cost
t-statistic above the same written bar as news_drift_v1
positive mean net excess in both chronological halves
fewer than 10% unscorable 30 trading days after the horizon
reported_not_criteria: VIX level at the signal (Nagel condition, logged)
result with and without the sector residual condition

open_choices: 1. Sector ETF map: nothing in the repo or in free point-in-time data maps a stock to a sector ETF. Options: (a) SIC code from the EDGAR submissions API (tempo.events_scan already caches it for event filers) mapped to the 11 SPDR sector ETFs by a table written now and frozen; coarse, wrong for conglomerates; (b) GICS sector from a public S&P 500 constituents file, mapped once to the SPDR ETFs, frozen with the universe. Recommended: (b), because the universe is already a frozen S&P 500 list.
2. Same headline-window and provider choices as news_drift_v1 (its open_choices 2).
3. Whether the 4% residual should be a fixed number or scaled by the stock's own 20-day volatility (vol20 is now logged on every signal): fixed is simpler and was the plan's wording.
known_limits: The absence of a headline in three feeds is not the absence of news: a missed story makes a fundamental move look like a liquidity move, and the fade then loses.
Long signals after a fall are the dangerous side if the news was simply not in these feeds.
if_fail: Report it as a failure; weekly_reversal_v1 stays as the only reversal test.
if_pass: Not proof and not real money: second period, realistic-size execution check, then evidence/gate.json.
